items.title: Hold an Arvada business license
items.description: Business licenses are free and do not expire (food trucks and short-term rentals renew annually); you keep the license active by filing the assigned sales and use tax returns.

items.title: Hold an Aurora business license
items.authority: City of Aurora Tax and Licensing Division
items.description: Any business operating in Aurora or with employees there needs a city business license, one per location. The license covers two years from issuance and establishes sales, use, occupational privilege and lodger's tax filing roles.

items.title: Hold and renew Boulder business licenses
items.authority: City of Boulder Tax and Licensing
items.description: Business licenses are issued site by site, applied for and renewed through the Boulder Online Tax System; businesses also hold a sales tax account in good standing.

items.title: Renew Centennial sales tax license or business registration
items.description: Every active business needs either a Retail Sales Tax License or a Business Registration (one, not both); both are biennial and expire December 31 of the second calendar year.
items.deadline: December 31 of the second calendar year

items.title: Hold Colorado Springs sales tax license
items.authority: City of Colorado Springs Sales Tax Office
items.description: Businesses selling or leasing at retail in the city need a city sales tax license (no fee since September 1, 2023). Licenses expire every odd year on December 31 and are renewed online only.

items.title: Obtain Denver sales and use tax license
items.authority: Denver Department of Finance, Treasury Division
items.description: Denver is a home-rule city and administers its own sales and use tax separately from the state.

items.title: Withhold and remit Denver Occupational Privilege Tax (OPT)
items.authority: Denver Department of Finance, Treasury Division
items.description: Employers and employees pay a monthly occupational privilege tax for work performed in Denver.
items.deadline: Monthly for employers with 10 or more employees; employers with fewer may file quarterly

feeDetail.note: Business OPT of $4.00 per month per taxable employee, owner or manager, plus $5.75 per month withheld from each taxable employee

items.title: Hold a Fort Collins sales and use tax license
items.authority: City of Fort Collins Sales Tax Office
items.description: The city's sales and use tax license serves as its business license, with no fee; each location needs its own, and a home occupation license is separate.

items.title: Obtain a Greeley business license
items.authority: City of Greeley Sales Tax Division
items.description: Any company or individual conducting business in Greeley must obtain a city business license; the official page lists license resources but does not state one universal renewal date.

items.title: Obtain a Greeley building permit when required
items.description: Greeley requires a building permit before covered construction, alteration, repair, demolition, or a change of occupancy begins.

items.title: Obtain a Greeley certificate of occupancy when required
items.description: Greeley requires completion of construction and required inspections before releasing permits or certificates of occupancy; a new certificate is issued when existing-building work changes the use.

items.title: Obtain a Lakewood, Colorado business license
items.description: Every business with a physical presence in Lakewood must have a city business license; the city also requires applicable business tax filings at the frequency assigned to the business.

items.title: Obtain a Lakewood, Colorado building permit when required
items.authority: City of Lakewood Public Works Department
items.description: Lakewood requires applicable building and construction permits before regulated work begins and processes permit fees and inspections through its permit system.

items.title: Obtain a Lakewood, Colorado certificate of occupancy when required
items.description: Lakewood issues a certificate of occupancy for new buildings and remodels involving a change in occupancy after required inspections; an active building permit is required for existing buildings.

items.title: Obtain a Pueblo sales and use tax license
items.authority: City of Pueblo Finance Department, Sales Tax Division
items.description: Businesses with a Pueblo location start routing through the city portal, then pay fees and apply for the sales and use tax license; returns are due the 20th of the month after the period.

items.title: Hold a Thornton sales and use tax business license
items.authority: City of Thornton Sales Tax Division
items.description: All businesses in Thornton need a city sales and use tax business license, free of charge and with no annual renewal; a certificate of occupancy is also required for locations.

items.title: Renew Westminster business license
items.authority: City of Westminster City Clerk and Sales Tax Division
items.description: Business and sales tax licenses renew annually through the online portal at no fee for commercial locations; a reminder email goes 60 days before expiration.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Longmont
items.description: Longmont requires businesses engaged in business in the city to obtain a Sales and Use Tax License; the one-time license fee is $25 and processing may take up to 10 working days.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Castle Rock
items.description: Castle Rock requires every business operating in town to obtain a business and tax license before opening; the application fee is $10 and approval may take at least two weeks.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Loveland
items.description: Loveland does not issue a general business license; businesses selling taxable goods or services need a City sales tax license, and the city's application lists a $20 application fee.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Broomfield
items.description: Broomfield does not require a separate general business license to operate, but businesses must register with the State of Colorado and may need city-issued liquor, tobacco, or solicitor licenses.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Commerce City
items.description: Commerce City requires every business, including service-only businesses, to obtain a general business license; the license does not require annual renewal, and additional specialty licenses may apply.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Grand Junction
items.description: Grand Junction requires businesses covered by city code to obtain the applicable license or permit and pay the specified license fee in advance of issuance; sales and use tax licenses require an application to Finance.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Parker
items.description: Parker requires businesses subject to its licensing rules to use the Town's business license application; the Town publishes current business-license fees and renewal information through its official forms and policies.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Littleton
items.description: Littleton requires businesses engaged in commerce within the city to register for a Business and Sales/Use Tax License; the application has no fee, and sales/use tax returns are due by the 20th of the following month.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Brighton
items.description: Brighton requires businesses with a physical presence in the city, including home-based businesses, to hold an active city business license; the general business and sales tax license has no application fee and renewals are reviewed by the city.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Windsor
items.description: Windsor requires businesses with a physical presence in town to obtain and renew a local business license; retailers without physical presence may qualify for Colorado's streamlined no-fee local-license process.
